ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, shareholders and transaction counterparties against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, FATF Public Statements, and Luxembourg domestic freezing measures. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified using risk-based procedures consistent with FATF Recommendation 12 and the 2004 AML Law as amended. The Luxembourg registered agent and/or the opening credit institution must document all screening results, obtain source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and file any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for the private equity buyout SPV because of the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and the use of syndicated loan wires and SWIFT payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MyLBR – Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS accepts corporate names written in the Latin alphabet; the name may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, English or another language, provided it employs Latin-script transliteration and is not misleading. All supporting documents submitted in another language must be accompanied by a certified French, German or Luxembourgish translation. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration and must not contravene Luxembourg public policy or positive law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Applicants may request a name reservation via the RCS/LBR portal before filing the notarial deed. A rejected or opposed name may be re-submitted with a modified version through the same portal. Where the refusal is administrative, the applicant or counsel may file a written reasoned re-examination request with the RCS Head Registrar. Judicial appeal lies before the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification of the refusal. If the name reservation has expired, a fresh reservation application can be made immediately; the notary should be instructed to reserve a backup name at the same time to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. Article 710-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915 requires a registered office in Luxembourg with a physical address. A shared office space or dedicated corporate-services address may satisfy the legal requirement only when actual business records are maintainable at that address and the entity has local substance indicators: local management meetings, Luxembourg-resident director capacity, locally retained accounts, and an economic presence proportionate to the private equity buyout activity. A fully-virtual mailbox without any local operational presence will expose the entity to UBO-register challenge, tax substance controversy, and reclassification risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS, CSSF, tax authorities or the financial intelligence unit is approximately 45% within the first 24 months after incorporation. The likelihood rises to 65% if the registered office is a mass-service address shared by numerous opaque SPVs or if the company lacks a Luxembourg-resident business manager.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended and consolidated, particularly Articles 180 et seq. applicable to the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (S.à r.l.), and implementing RCS registration regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operational through the www.lbr.lu electronic filing portal and the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial act of incorporation (acte constitutif) incorporating the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of EUR 12,000.00, fully subscribed and paid in cash before incorporation; the funds must be deposited into a blocked escrow account opened in the name of the future S.à r.l. with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution, and may be released only after production of the RCS registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers shall receive the share capital allocations set forth in the bylaws and the paid-up capital deposits shall remain in escrow until the RCS certificate is issued. RESOLVED, that the temporary registered office is adopted as set forth in the constitutive act, and all statutory books and seals shall be maintained there. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] are appointed manager(s) of the company, each vested with full authority to open bank accounts, sign loan and equity documents, instruct counsel, and represent the company before the RCS, subject to a joint signature threshold of EUR [amount] for PE syndicate transactions. RESOLVED, that the manager(s) are authorized to execute all filings and publish the formation notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and reservation with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / LBR electronic filing portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the LBR portal, submit the proposed corporate name and legal form S.à r.l., and request a name clearance. The request is processed in the ordinary course of one business day; retain the clearance reference for use in the notarial deed and bank escrow account opening.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate legal form S.à r.l.
Identity documents of the prospective shareholder(s) and manager(s)
Description of corporate object mapping to ISIC 6499 private equity buyout acquisition investments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is queried or rejected for conflict, promptly submit three alternative names with a covering letter explaining the PE buyout SPV structure; RCS generally resolves the resubmission within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked escrow share-capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg or EEA licensed credit institution selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the future S.à r.l. and deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000.00. The bank must issue a certificate confirming the deposit and blocked status, and agree that funds will only be released against the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming deposit and blocked status
Draft constitutive act and articles for bank KYC
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and corporate chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership, supply a full corporate structure chart and passport copies of relevant natural persons; funds remain blocked pending receipt of the RCS certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association. Convene the subscribers and intended managers for execution; the notary verifies identities, certifies payment of the share capital, and, after execution, transmits the electronic filing package to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Name clearance receipt from LBR
Bank certificate validating escrowed share capital
Passports or national identity cards of all identified parties
Final version of the articles of association
Shareholders' side letters or investment management agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises queries on the draft, amend the articles and re-execute a rectification deed; any correction affecting share capital must be supported by an updated released escrow certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration filing with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS Registration Department (Guichet unique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or counsel files the signed electronic incorporation file through the RCS online submission portal, pays the applicable official state filing fee, and tracks the application until the RCS assigns the business registration number and issues the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Electronically executed notarial deed and articles
Bank certificate attesting paid-up capital
Identity forms for managers and shareholders
Power of attorney or counsel engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a rectifying annex and a written explanation to the RCS; refiling may incur a minor supplementary fee, and the existing escrow certificate remains valid if unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of formation notice in the official electronic companies register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Publications (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, ensure that the mandatory legal publication of formation appears in RESA, including the registered office, manager(s), and corporate object. Retain the official publication proof for the corporate governing file and banking counterparties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Corporate object and officer details as validated in the notarial deed
Contact details of the authorized legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is suspended or rejected due to data discrepancy, verify the LBR data, file a corrected notice with the RCS, and republish; an updated excerpt is then available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration filing in the beneficial ownership register (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the required beneficial ownership declaration within 30 days of registration through the RBE portal. Identify every natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of the S.à r.l. and maintain the register status for AML and PE syndicate governance purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
UBO identification documents and passport copies
Control structure chart identifying PE syndicate ultimate individuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is queried, resubmit a corrected UBO declaration with accompanying legal evidence; failure to cure promptly may expose the company to administrative fines and public non-compliance notices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial operating license required for a private equity buyout special purpose vehicle.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the S.à r.l. will act solely as a holding and financing SPV under ISIC 6499 and will not operate a physical facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical project or facility is carried out by this PE buyout SPV; no EIA registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge, air emissions, VOC emissions, or waste handling occur as part of the registered object; if a portfolio company later conducts physical operations, EIA requirements will be assessed separately at entity level.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — the SPV has only a registered office with no employees, no manufacturing facility, no structural loading, and no such activity requiring fire safety certification, occupational clearance, or civil defense licensing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and stamp taxes; Customs and Excise Agency (Administration des douanes et accises, ADN) for customs and excise. Electronic filing and taxpayer portals: myTax.lu, MyGuichet.lu, and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary and file the notarial deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the RCS registration number and matricule, which is the master corporate identifier for all tax accounts. 2) Apply for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA, 'LU' + 8 digits) electronically via MyGuichet.lu on AEDT Form 106 as soon as taxable supplies commence; a non-resident entity without a Luxembourg establishment making taxable supplies must register directly with the AEDT and, if established outside the EEA, appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative. 3) Obtain an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Agency (ADN) for all customs import/export formalities. 4) The corporate income tax and municipal business tax accounts are set up automatically from the RCS registration; annual tax returns are filed under the RCS/matricule reference. 5) If the SPV has employees or payroll, register separately with the Luxembourg Social Security Centre (CCSS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the SARL is an opaque juridical person subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur la collectivités) on worldwide income, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and annual net wealth tax; it has unlimited tax liability as a Luxembourg tax resident. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Luxembourg domestic law, and a US 'check-the-box' election has no effect on Luxembourg entity classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election allowing a 95%+ resident parent and its subsidiaries to be treated as one taxable entity for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; optional VAT group (assujetti unique) election for closely connected taxable persons under the transposed EU VAT Directive; participation exemption election under the 10% shareholding / 12-month holding condition; no domestic check-the-box election exists; hybrid mismatch elections are neutralized by Luxembourg ATAD implementation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979, transposing the EU VAT Directive
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general compulsory turnover threshold: any taxable person carrying on a taxable supply of goods or services in Luxembourg must register for VAT, subject to the optional small-business franchise exemption of EUR 30,000 annual turnover; non-established EU traders registering under the OSS/Distance Sales scheme benefit from the EUR 10,000 intra-Community distance-selling threshold; intra-Community acquisitions by non-taxable persons are subject to a EUR 10,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg. Electronic VAT filing and EC sales listings are mandatory through the AEDT e-filing portal (myTax/eTVA). E-invoicing is mandatory only for B2G public procurement via the national PEPPOL infrastructure in Factur-X/BIS format since 1 March 2020; private B2B e-invoicing remains optional and subject to recipient consent, with paper and PDF invoices still legally accepted for non-public supply chains.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for the 0% VAT rate where the supplier proves, through the export customs declaration and transport documentation, that the goods physically left the EU within 3 months of the supply. Certain internationally-linked services are also zero-rated, notably sea and air transport of goods, related loading/unloading and ancillary handling services, and services directly performed on movable goods destined for export. Cross-border B2B services are outside Luxembourg VAT scope and shift to the recipient under reverse charge. For a private equity buyout SPV, pure financial and fund-management services are VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated; such exempt services can be structured through separate cost-bearing entities to optimize irrecoverable VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/EX) lodged electronically in the Luxembourg AES/ECS customs system
Bill of Lading (sea), CMR (road), Air Waybill (air) or postal/courier receipt evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward remittance certificate or bank transfer confirmation evidencing receipt of the export consideration
Certificate of Origin or EUR.1 movement certificate, if preferential tariff treatment is claimed
Incoterms-based sale contract and order documentation substantiating the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts targeted documentary audits on high-risk export zero-rating claims; insufficient or inconsistent proof triggers retroactive VAT assessment with statutory interest. The standard limitation period is 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraud or deliberate evasion. Fraudulent zero-rating exposes the taxpayer to full clawback of the VAT, late-payment interest, penalties up to 100% of the evaded tax, administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000, and criminal prosecution (including imprisonment) under Luxembourg tax-fraud provisions; the burden of substantiating the export and the repatriation of consideration rests entirely on the supplier.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential supervision of credit institutions delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The BCL operates TARGET2-Luxembourg settlement, manages euro monetary operations, collects balance-of-payments statistics under Regulation (EC) No 184/2005, and co-owns the domestic AML/CFT framework with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and CSSF.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised euro area jurisdiction. The euro (EUR) is freely convertible on both current and capital account; Articles 63-66 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC guarantee free movement of capital. No exchange control approval, no convertibility restrictions, and no profit remittance licences apply to non-resident investors. Dividends, redemption proceeds, liquidation surpluses and loan repayments can be remitted abroad without BCL authorisation, subject only to corporate law formalities (notarised shareholder resolutions, statutory audit where legal thresholds are exceeded), the 15% domestic dividend withholding tax (reducible by treaty or the Luxembourg participation exemption provisions) and bank-side BOP statistical declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for trade receipts. The BCL requires only statistical balance-of-payments reporting for cross-border settlements. For a private equity buyout SPV under ISIC 6499, there is no export trade cycle; acquisition financing, capital call subscriptions and disposal proceeds must be identified in SWIFT remittance fields as financial-account BOP categories (F.1 direct investment equity, F.112 direct investment loans) rather than trade-related receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability with significant legal constraints. CSSF-authorised or EU-passported electronic money institutions (Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services) can provide a Luxembourg IBAN operational account and low-value administrative disbursements. However, an EMI cannot act as settlement account provider for syndicated loan wires, cannot directly hold client escrow without a BCL-licensed sponsoring credit institution, and has no direct TARGET2 access. Non-EEA offshore EMIs lack EU passporting rights and will be declined by Luxembourg banks for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced PE vehicle. The blueprint permits EMIs solely for pre-funding professional fees and operating expenses, while all acquisition capital, escrow and clearing balances remain on domestic Tier-1 banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial onboarding. Under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02, the credit institution must conduct an in-person CDD interview with at least one authorised manager (gérant) or a duly appointed Luxembourg-resident representative before the account is activated; pure remote video onboarding is not accepted as the primary client meeting for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced entity. The required interview may be discharged by a Luxembourg lawyer, accountant or regulated fiduciary holding a notarised power of attorney, provided the agent appears physically and the ultimate economic owners documentation is independently certified. All UBOs with 25% or greater interest undergo individual CDD; certified passport copies, proof of address, source-of-wealth statements and a signed PEP questionnaire may be completed via CSSF-approved video-identification as a supplementary layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque investor chain (offshore feeder funds, discretionary nominees, layered holding vehicles within the acquisition syndicate).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date RCS Luxembourg corporate extracts; notarised certificates of incorporation for every upstream holding vehicle; the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) filing certificate under the Law of 13 January 2019; a fund administrator or Big-Four certified ownership chart; placement memorandum and subscription agreements; reference letter of the regulated fund administrator; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for all material investors; tax residence certificates; and a signed AML self-assessment questionnaire mapping economic ownership down to natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited substance indicators: registered office at a mass-services address, no local management activity, no operational turnover, and formation of a SARL with only the EUR 12,000 statutory minimum capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease with proof of physical occupancy; management services agreement with a Luxembourg corporate-services provider supported by invoicing history; board minutes and manager appointment resolutions; Luxembourg VAT registration certificate; quarterly BCL BOP statistical filings; evidence of active bank payment flow; transaction budget and business plan for the LBO acquisition; and a substance memo prepared by local counsel confirming management oversight in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalisation and high-velocity intercompany loan flows (capital call financing, shareholder bridging loans, target debt pushdowns).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised bank capital deposit certificate evidencing subscription payment; shareholder resolution approving the capital increase; intercompany loan agreements with arm's length interest rate and repayment schedule; indicative acquisition debt term sheet from the senior lender; capital call notices and LBO financial model; audited or interim annual accounts; and a forward-looking cash-flow forecast aligned with committed acquisition milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-country-risk exposure in the target portfolio or financing syndicate (unexpected PEP involvement, financing flows touching non-cooperative FATF jurisdictions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction pipeline and target corporate certificates; output of vendor-based sanctions screening on all counterparties; PEP declarations for all financing parties; notarised undertakings that no funds originate from sanctioned persons or institutions; a dedicated compliance note from the relationship bank documenting internal risk acceptance; statements from target management confirming share provenance; and an EU/EEA counsel engagement letter narrating each cross-border flow and its legitimate economic rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections arrive via SWIFT MT103/MT202 into the EUR operational or escrow account, with field 70 remittance information stating the notarised capital subscription deed reference or shareholder loan agreement reference, the beneficiary account number, funding jurisdiction code, and the ECB BOP classification. Equity contributions must be coded as F.1 (direct investment equity); shareholder loans as F.112 (direct investment loans). Funds can be injected as equity (notarised capital increase registered with the RCS) or as documented shareholder loans with arm's length interest. For each injection exceeding EUR 10,000, the bank requires a written facility agreement or notarised deed, pre-cleared with the relationship manager; the BCL quarterly BOP declaration is automatically generated by the bank from these remittance classifications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement flows use three clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for purchase price payments, capital distribution and fund disbursements; (ii) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV for interbank cover payments; and (iii) commercial or standby letters of credit (MT700 under UCP 600/ISP98) for post-closing price adjustments, warranty collateral or vendor securities. EUR payments clear through TARGET2-Luxembourg or SEPA Instant for EEA counterparties; USD and GBP leg settlement occurs through correspondent banking chains. Every disbursement requires a transaction purpose code in field 70 referencing the underlying acquisition agreement, the BOP classification (equity sell-down, dividend distribution, shareholder loan repayment), and the tax clearing certificate where withholding obligations apply. The standard buyout closing timetable is T+1 wire release after same-day funding confirmation and internal compliance clearance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) executed bilaterally under ISDA or standard forward confirmation, collateralised under a credit support annex where tenor exceeds one year
Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDF) on restricted-currency exposures (CNY, INR, BRL, IDR, KRW) referenced to ECB or WM/Refinitiv fixings and executed through a global FX prime broker
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with credit support annex to convert USD-denominated acquisition debt into EUR cash flow profiles
Plain vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars for hedging committed future equity purchases or binding purchase price exposure between signature and closing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex; abbreviated form available for small SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS/LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL: shareholder approval within 6 months after year-end (by 30 June) and filing with RCS within 1 month after approval, in no case later than 7 months after year-end (by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may lead to administrative penalties and fines imposed on managers, court-ordered filing, and after two consecutive years of non-filing and formal notice, administrative strike-off from the RCS and dissolution; directors may also incur civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data (registered office, managers, object, corporate details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS/LBR (electronic via eJustice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of the company's RCS registration each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm may trigger a formal reminder and penalty for continued non-compliance; persistent omission can obstruct issuance of RCS certificates and contribute to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE/LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed no later than 31 March of each calendar year; any change to beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing exposes the SARL and managers to administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 and/or criminal sanctions (EUR 500 to EUR 125,000, imprisonment for managing officers in serious cases); repeated failure may trigger enforcement notices and regulatory escalation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 611) including municipal business tax and annexed tax accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD / Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year tax periods: statutory filing by 31 May of the following year; automatic extension until 31 December where the return is prepared by an accredited tax adviser or filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing can trigger monthly 0.7% interest on unpaid tax, late-filing penalties up to 10% of the tax, tax assessment ex officio, and seizure; deliberate non-filing may give rise to criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (Form 612) and payment of annual net wealth tax, including minimum net wealth tax for financial undertakings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline aligned to the corporate income tax return (31 May standard, 31 December with tax adviser extension); tax is payable on assessment or by semi-annual instalments as directed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid net wealth tax accrues 0.7% per month interest and may be increased by penalties up to 10%; enforcement comprises forced collection over assets and director liability for non-declaration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory if, for two consecutive years, the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4m, net turnover > EUR 8.8m, and average workforce > 50 employees. Audit is also required for public-interest and regulated entities; otherwise the SARL may be audit-exempt but must still prepare, approve, and file annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002 on companies and accounting obligations and EU accounting directives; IFRS may be used for consolidated reporting and is not required for the standalone SARL unless the group elects it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file any change in beneficial ownership with the RBE within one month of the relevant share transfer or control event. In addition, an annual confirmation of the recorded beneficial owners is compulsory and must be filed electronically by 31 March of each year, confirming either no change or the corrected data. The filing must be signed by the managing director or authorised representative; access to the RBE is restricted to Luxembourg authorities and AML-identified professionals.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / nominal share register (registre des associés)
Minute Book of shareholder and management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,800 per year (typical Luxembourg registered office and corporate agent fee range for a small SARL SPV)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 18,000 per year for a full statutory audit of a small PE SPV; no audit fee is incurred if the company is audit-exempt and no audit is voluntarily appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT + municipal business tax, Luxembourg City rate 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% shareholding or ≥€1.2M acquisition cost, held ≥12 months); IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income); notional interest deduction for equity financing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 1001 (Net Wealth Tax Return) filed via eCDF (Electronic Corporate Tax Filing) or MyGuichet portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 31 December if filed electronically; further extension possible upon request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax ID and permanent establishment details if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the accounting period; non-residents with PE must align with PE's fiscal year
Compute Luxembourg-source income attributable to PE; apply DTA provisions to avoid double taxation
Claim exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; attach supporting documentation (shareholding %, holding period)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax base (unitary value of assets)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with PE are subject to net wealth tax on Luxembourg-situs assets; minimum net wealth tax applies

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 per month (max €2,500); late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties up to 10% of tax due for gross negligence

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (standard rate); 0% under participation exemption if conditions met (≥10% shareholding or ≥€1.2M acquisition cost, held ≥12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced WHT under a DTA, the beneficial owner must submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence state and a Form 105 (or equivalent) to the Luxembourg tax administration before or at the time of dividend distribution; the payer must retain documentation for audit purposes
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory (except for certain profit-participating loans); Royalties: 15% statutory, reduced to 0% under most DTAs (e.g., EU Interest & Royalty Directive) if beneficial owner is EU resident and meets 25% shareholding threshold

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File required if group consolidated revenue ≥ €50 million and related-party transactions exceed €1 million; CbC report required if group revenue ≥ €750 million
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for certain activities (banking, insurance, distribution, service centers, financing, leasing, holding companies); PE SPVs must demonstrate substance (office, employees, decision-making) to avoid being classified as shell and to benefit from tax treaty and EU directives

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial transactions, sham arrangements, or deliberate misreporting of taxable income to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 or 10% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution for fraud; additional penalties up to 100% of tax due
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for civil restitution of unpaid taxes; travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years for willful evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No physical presence, no employees, no real economic activity, or passive holding without substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, participation exemption, and EU directives; reclassification of income; penalty up to €250,000; mandatory liquidation if deemed abusive
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly operated a shell; travel bans and asset freezes possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining adequate records under Luxembourg AML law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering (up to 5 years imprisonment)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from serving as directors
